    • nextNode

      public org.conetex.runtime.instrument.collection.AvlTree.AbstractNode<K,V> nextNode()
      Returns the next node in reverse in-order traversal and advances the iterator.

      If the iterator has no more elements this method returns null (the implementation does not throw NoSuchElementException).

      The returned value is the internal AbstractNode<K,V> representing the next element; callers can use key() and value() on the returned node. The iterator's internal stack is advanced so subsequent calls continue the reverse traversal.

      Note: the result reflects the iterator's state at the time of the call and may become invalid if the underlying tree is modified concurrently.

      Returns:
      the next AbstractNode<K,V> in descending (reverse in-order) order, or null if none

    • hasNext

      public final boolean hasNext()
      Returns true if the reverse-order iterator has more elements to yield.

      This method inspects the iterator's internal stack to determine whether there are remaining nodes to traverse in reverse in-order sequence.

      Note: the result reflects the iterator's current state and may change if the underlying tree is modified concurrently. The iterator's methods are not safe for concurrent modification without external synchronization.

      Returns:
      true if there is at least one more element available, false otherwise
